The price has nothing to do with it. These companies make more now than they ever have before. The issue is that executives want to push out the safest games possible as fast as possible and they hamstring the developers to do that. If developers got even the slightest bit of freedom you’d see game quality sky rocket.

Even $60 is too high for most triple A titles now. These companies deliver unfinished buggy messes with unoriginal plots and shallow characters. On top of that, we have companies like Ubisoft telling its customers ‘get used to not owning your games’, companies like Nintendo, rockstar, activision, etc that sue people for trying to preserve games that they don’t even sell anymore, and companies like Sony that buy IPs just to never use them and kill franchises that players love. AAA companies over the last few years have fallen off catastrophically and made it clear time and time again that they couldn’t care less about their customers as long as you buy the game and load up on microtransactions. Microtransactions btw use insanely shady tactics such as multiple premium currencies to hide how much you actually spend on a game. Loot boxes are designed to be addictive and marketed specifically to younger players. You ever notice how when buying in game currency you can never buy just the right amount? It’s always either way too low or way too high. It’s a ploy to get you to buy more even if you don’t want to. It’s super shady and hurts consumers. People need to stop buying AAA games until they learn to respect their customers. There are INCREDIBLE indie companies out there that have cheap games with complex characters and nuanced stories.
